sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house fast in Baytown, TX?
sections.html:
Baytown homeowners can list with a real estate agent, sell the house on their own, or sell to a cash buyer who takes the house as-is. Cash sales appeal most to owners with a repair backlog, an inherited house, a tenant they want to move on from, or a deadline set by a lender or a court.

The city has 86,561 estimated residents as of July 1, 2025, and 52.3 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, based on the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates. With a median home value of $197,300, Baytown sits at a price level where repair costs can take a large share of what a listed house nets.

  • Agent listing: a good fit for a house in solid condition, with time for showings and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Owner sale: you take on pricing, contracts and buyer questions, then close through a title company.
  • Cash buyer: no lender, no repair list, and a closing date you negotiate, usually after a short walk-through.

sections.h2: How did Baytown grow around the refinery, and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Baytown grew around oil and chemical plants east of Houston, and many neighborhoods trace back to employer-built housing and mid-century expansion. The Texas State Historical Association describes a highly industrialized city of refineries, rubber, chemical and carbon black plants, thirty miles east of downtown Houston on Interstate 10 and State Highway 146.

An oil strike in 1908 and the Goose Creek field, the first offshore drilling in Texas in 1916, set the stage. In 1917 the founders of Humble Oil and Refining bought about 2,200 acres and began building a refinery in 1919. The company laid out streets, provided utilities, sold lots and financed homes for employees, which made the settlement permanent by 1923. Pelly, Goose Creek and the Baytown company site consolidated, and the city of Baytown was established on January 24, 1948.

Population climbed from 20,958 in 1948 to 67,117 in 1990, and the city grew from 7.5 square miles to more than 32. The Census Bureau lists 37.00 square miles of land in 2020. The Baytown-La Porte Tunnel opened in 1953 and the Fred Hartman Bridge replaced it in the mid-1990s. Lee College and a large regional mall are among the institutions the Handbook lists.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Baytown?
sections.html:
Median gross rent in Baytown was $1,307 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and median owner costs were $1,761 a month with a mortgage and $691 without. Median household income was $59,910 in 2024 dollars, and 18.2 percent of residents were in poverty.

Growth has been modest lately: the city is up 1.2 percent from the 2020 estimates base of 85,547, after rising from 71,802 in 2010 to 83,701 in 2020. Of residents 25 and older, 78.6 percent finished high school and 14.8 percent hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

sections.h2: Which county handles my Baytown property, Harris or Chambers?
sections.html:
It depends on where the parcel sits. Baytown lies in southeastern Harris County, and its boundaries reach east into Chambers County, so two sets of county offices serve the city.

That split matters at closing. The deed is recorded with the county clerk of the county where the land is located, the county appraisal district sets the value, and the county tax assessor-collector often bills for the taxing units. A seller should look at the tax statement for the exact account number and county, because a search of the wrong county will turn up nothing.

  • Check the top of your tax bill for the county and the appraisal district account.
  • Ask the title company which county clerk will record the deed.
  • If you live near the line between the two counties, confirm which school and other taxing districts appear on the bill.

The Comptroller's property tax basics page explains that appraisal districts set values as of January 1 and that the assessor-collector bills around October 1.

sections.h2: Can I rent a Baytown house by the night, and does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Baytown has allowed short-term rentals in residential and mixed-use zoning districts only with a Special Use Permit from City Council. The first such permit came before Council on December 11, 2025, and was approved with conditions for an existing house in a Suburban Residential district.

City staff then proposed a text amendment to the Unified Land Development Code that would drop the Special Use Permit and allow short-term rentals through a permit process in the same districts. The planning commission hearing was set for March 17, 2026, and City Council's hearing for April 23, 2026. Council also reviewed ideas such as annual permits and inspections and limits on occupancy and parking.

If your house has been used for nightly stays, ask the Baytown planning staff which rule applies to the address and whether any permit exists. A buyer who counts on rental income should confirm the approval status with the city before signing. The city's code amendment notice describes the proposal.

sections.h2: How do I sell an inherited house in Baytown?
sections.html:
Start by working out how title passes, since that decides what the title company will accept. Texas allows a will to be probated within four years of death, and a court may accept a later filing for an acceptable reason.

  • Muniment of title: available when the estate owes nothing except liens on real estate. The court order and the will are filed with the county clerk where the property sits.
  • Small estate affidavit: for estates with assets of $75,000 or less, not counting the homestead and exempt property. It generally cannot cover real property other than a homestead passing to a spouse or minor children.
  • Affidavit of heirship: a sworn statement filed with the clerk. No law forces a title company to accept it.
  • Executor's or administrator's deed: used when a court has appointed a personal representative.

Heirs who are not named on a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim a homestead exemption on an inherited home. The Texas State Law Library's probate guide describes each route, and a probate attorney can tell you which fits your family.

sections.h2: What if the house has unpaid taxes or a lien?
sections.html:
A tax lien attaches to a Baytown property each January 1 and follows it through a sale, so the balance is paid at closing from the seller's proceeds. Bills go out in October, and in most cases taxes unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest that keep adding up.

A homestead owner who is behind may be able to arrange an installment plan with the collector, and some collectors allow up to 36 months. A waiver of penalty and interest is possible in limited cases when the tax is paid within 21 days of learning of the delinquency and the request is made in writing within 181 days of the delinquency date. Ask the tax assessor-collector for a payoff figure before you set a closing date, and have the title company confirm that no other judgment or lien shows on the title.

faqs.q: Does Baytown sit in Harris County or Chambers County?
faqs.a: Both. The city is in southeastern Harris County and extends east into Chambers County. Confirm the county on your tax bill, because that county's clerk records your deed and its appraisal district values the property.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Baytown?
faqs.a: Baytown's code has required a Special Use Permit approved by City Council, and a 2026 amendment proposed replacing it with a permit process. Contact the planning staff for the rule that applies to your address before you tell a buyer the house can be used for short stays.

faqs.q: How long can I wait to probate a will before selling an inherited Baytown house?
faqs.a: A will generally must be filed for probate within four years of death, though a court can accept a later filing for good reason. If the estate qualifies for a muniment of title, the court order and the will go to the county clerk where the property is located.

faqs.q: What is the typical value of a Baytown home?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts the median value of owner-occupied housing units at $197,300 for 2020-2024. That is a city-wide median, so your house can fall well above or below it depending on size, age and condition.
Baytown had an estimated 86,561 residents on July 1, 2025, up 1.2 percent from the 2020 estimates base. It covers 37.00 square miles of land and had 30,964 households in the 2020-2024 survey.
